builds.name: Reference: Range and poke
builds.goal: Reference for Lux: establish a repeatable reference
builds.hypothesis: A ranged catch mage who zones with E, roots two targets with Q and cashes spell marks through attacks or her laser. Separate E/Q/R spell burst, passive-mark consumption by a real attack and allied shield value. Lich Bane requires stepping into attack range safely. Range-compatible spell hits test poke AP/penetration before a commitment.
builds.summary: Range-compatible spell hits test poke AP/penetration before a commitment.
testPlan: Kit question for Lux: Separate E/Q/R spell burst, passive-mark consumption by a real attack and allied shield value. Lich Bane requires stepping into attack range safely.

Start with the early core (Luden, then Horizon) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Use this as the control for the other three routes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Range-compatible spell hits test poke AP/penetration before a commitment. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern.

Q evidence: Lux releases a sphere of light that binds and deals damage to up to two enemy units. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Comet can miss and distance matters; no automatic full-range damage bonus.
The route fails Lux's stated kit question: Separate E/Q/R spell burst, passive-mark consumption by a real attack and allied shield value. Lich Bane requires stepping into attack range safely.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Comet can miss and distance matters; no automatic full-range damage bonus.
Full cost 16,050 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
The reference is a research control, not a claim of the current highest-win-rate build.
buyOrder: Luden, then Horizon. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff, Banshee's Veil are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

builds.name: Double Pass Charge Heal
builds.summary: Log two shield passes and Helia consumption per pass.
builds.goal: Log two shield passes and Helia consumption per pass.
builds.hypothesis: W shields allies on outward and return passes. Q/E champion damage can preload Helia before W, while Staff gives AP/haste on allied shielding; AP improves both shield passes. Q immobilization can supply Mandate vulnerability to support the ally's damage.
testPlan: Required state: An ally intersects both W paths after champion damage and Q hits for Mandate.
Log two shield passes and Helia consumption per pass; repeat at equal gold, finite stacks, same ranks and defenses against a moving target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Return path misses the ally or charges were already consumed.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Two shield passes do not prove two full independent Helia heals.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Echoes of Helia, Staff of Flowing Water, Imperial Mandate, Rabadon's Deathcap, Redemption, Ionian Boots of Lucidity. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Spark Mark Reload
builds.summary: Count marks consumed during Q-attack-R-attack sequence.
builds.goal: Count marks consumed during Q-attack-R-attack sequence.
builds.hypothesis: P says R consumes existing Illumination and refreshes it. Q/root enables an attack before R and a second attack after R; Lich Bane/Nashor reward the risky short-range weave while Cosmic/E slow can preserve access. AP keeps R and mark damage relevant.
testPlan: Required state: Target survives first attack/R and Lux can safely reach for refreshed mark.
Count marks consumed during Q-attack-R-attack sequence; repeat at equal gold, finite stacks, same ranks and defenses against a moving target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Approaching for two attacks forfeits range advantage or the target dies before the second mark.

tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: R refresh does not grant unlimited marks or free attack resets.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
